name: Digital arrest — authority impersonation with legal threat and payment demand
description: A sender claiming law-enforcement or government identity accuses the recipient of a crime, threatens arrest or asset seizure, and demands an immediate payment framed as a fine, security deposit or verification transfer. The combination is the pattern; no single element is decisive.

source_references.document_ref: Digital Arrest: The Modern-Day Cyber Scam (2025-04)
source_references.quote: Digital arrest is a scam designed to extort money from victims using fear, deceit, and intimidation.

lifecycle.$comment_separation_of_duties: Authoring and approval are the same person at team size 1 (ASM-019). The workflow is modelled and tested with distinct roles; it is not organisationally enforced during development.

explanation.plain: Someone claiming to be from the police or a government department has accused you of a crime and asked you to pay money. Indian law-enforcement agencies do not arrest people over a video call, and they never ask for a payment to clear your name. You are not required to pay, and you are allowed to tell your family.
explanation.technical: Matched AUTHORITY_IMPERSONATION with a coercion indicator and a payment demand, spanning three evidence classes (identity claim, pressure, payment action). NITI Aayog documents this exact sequence as extortion.
verification_steps: No Indian agency conducts arrests, interrogations or fine collection over a video or phone call.
Call the National Cyber Crime Helpline on 1930 to check any claim made against you.
Tell a family member now — isolation from family is part of the method, not a legal requirement.

provenance.notes: SRC-012's own wording is 'instructed not to involve family or lawyers'; the paraphrase 'secrecy' is not used by the source (D6) and is not encoded. Isolation is handled by TL-AUTH-002.
